identity.real_world_identity_notes: GT1 car built for Le Mans around a twin-turbo 3.5 litre V8, with the road-going homologation special sharing its name. Power reaches the rear wheels through an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox worked by a short-throw gear lever, which matches the sequential stick seen in the cockpit rather than paddles.

NISMO's official motorsport history identifies Nissan's 1998 R390 GT1 as the long-tail revision and says its transmission changed to a Nissan-built sequential type. Nissan's Heritage material identifies the R390 GT1 family and a six-speed sequential gearbox, while the 1998 Le Mans chassis R8 report identifies the race car and its cockpit. The exact PMR telemetry name and GT1 class are consistent with that existing curated identity; no separate real-world R390 variant is needed.

driver_summary: The Nissan R390 GT1, which Assetto Corsa lists as LMGT Nisumo R39 V8. Xtrac six-speed sequential on a short-throw lever. Upshift flat, the car cuts. It does not blip, so rev-match the downshifts yourself: a blip settles the rear into a corner whether or not the box demands it.
